classification.difficultyReason: Relate the graphs by reflection in the x-axis and explain why reversing the inequality when multiplying by minus one preserves the selected x-values.

inlines.text: . The relevant parabolas are shown below.
How are the two representations related? Does it make sense that the solution set is the same?

spec.description: Supplied downward-opening parabola y=9−x², with unit x-grid, two-unit y-grid, open intercepts and green interior solution region.
spec.mathematics: Vertex (0,9); intercepts (−3,0) and (3,0); x from −5 to 5, y from −16 to 10.

spec.description: Supplied upward-opening parabola y=x²−9, with unit x-grid, two-unit y-grid, open intercepts and the same green interior solution region.
spec.mathematics: Vertex (0,−9); intercepts (−3,0) and (3,0); x from −5 to 5, y from −10 to 16.

answer.short: The graphs are reflections in the $x$-axis. Multiplying by $-1$ also reverses the inequality sign, so both solution sets are $-3<x<3$.
answer.worked: Since $x^2-9=-(9-x^2)$, the graphs are reflections in the $x$-axis. Multiplying $9-x^2>0$ by $-1$ reverses the inequality sign and gives $x^2-9<0$. The first graph is above the $x$-axis exactly where the second is below it: $-3<x<3$. The endpoints are excluded because both inequalities are strict.
